notes.title: Transport games sale on Steam has begun!
notes.content:
Our studio has projects of different genres and themes in its portfolio. But our largest and most highly rated games are dedicated to transport: buses, trains and airplanes. Today, Planes, Trains, and Automobiles Fest starts on Steam. We are participating with three main games:

[b]About buses: Bus World.[/b] This is not another bus driver simulation game, but a unique experience in which you will face natural and man-made disasters. Although for lovers of quiet trips and scheduled flights, the game will also be able to please, because it has a Free Mode!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1193090/Bus_World/

[b]About airplanes: Fly Corp.[/b] This minimalistic, but extremely addictive transport strategy has already managed to charm the hearts of players from all over the world. Hop in and try to create a successful transport network!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1372530/Fly_Corp/

[b]About trains: Metro Simulator 2.[/b] The game boasts detailed recreations of real Metro stations and tunnels, as well as a realistic train control system.

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1787480/Metro_Simulator_2/

If you are already familiar with one of our games, we invite you to try out the others, because all of them have generous discounts.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41417136/c29c575d85f0fcf1b76173cc02c96ec60c4b7837.png[/img]

Enjoy your trips!

notes.title: Vote for Metro Simulator 2 at Steam Awards!
notes.content:
[h2]The autumn sale on Steam has begun, where you can purchase Metro Simulator 2 at a 70% discount![/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41417136/4770d059917797029f658c68732a1d3bba85142e.png[/img]

By the way, the annual Steam Awards nomination also starts today, where the best games of the year are selected in certain categories, and each of you can vote and influence the outcome.
The best reward for a developer is recognition from players, and that is why we invite you to take part in the Steam Awards too.

So, you come home after hard work and want to relax. There are many ways to do this and our game is one of the most original. Sit in a chair, switching toggle switches and buttons, set the train in motion. Outside the window, traffic lights and other tunnel objects pass by, one station gives way to another, and thousands of people rush about their business. Everything works like clockwork. 

We nominate Metro Simulator 2 for the title "Sit Back And Relax". [b]Help us by voting for our games![/b]

For us, our highest goal has always been and remains to continue to delight players around the world with high-quality and interesting projects, and we are very pleased to receive positive feedback from you.

notes.title: More news about scenarios
notes.content:
We're now almost finished with the two tutorial scenarios. All bugs that were found in them are fixed, but we're still testing them to make sure we won't find more over time. After that, we'll concentrate on two regular scenarios. They are already playable, but they have some bugs which we need to fix. It shouldn't take long.

Recently, we made a small feature: lights on Oka train now dim when you enter the station and get back to bright mode when you leave it.

Added achievements to the game, eight of them to be precise.

Now we'll try to implement mirrors on stations. Performance problems are likely, so they will be optional and disabled by default.

On the previous week, we sent in-game texts for translation to the languages which are used in countries with the largest number of players added the game to their wishlist. Also, we're starting our work on Early Access trailer.

In general, not much work is left to be done until Early Access release. We'll announce the precise date later.

notes.title: The new look of the old soviet train
notes.content:
This year is, probably, the hardest one ever for KishMish Games. Only in the first half of 2022, we faced lots of challenges which we neverd dealt with before. You already know about problems with payments due to restrictions. But also, this spring we received a complaint from one of the companies related to transport. They require us to pay a fine and remove content which is used illegally, in their opinion. We are still trying to insist that we aren't violating any copyrights, but it isn't a quick routine, and of course it takes money, time and mental health. It is still unknown what will happen in the end of this story.

In this regard, we took a decision that the new train in Metro Simulator 2 will look unlike any real train to minimize the risk of receiving more complaints. You can see its look on the screenshots (but not everything is set up, so this is not the final look). Anticipating questions about licensing a real train: our probability to negotiate on acceptable conditions is very low. We have some experience in working with lawyers in this sphere and representatives of transport companies. Unfortunately, situation with patents and copyrights in sphere of transport is very complicated: areas of responsibility of employees are blurred, taking decisions lasts for a long time and finally, they are not interested in cooperation with small studios like us due to non-comparable level of companies.

We understand that many of you may be disappointed with this news, but unfortunately there is nothing we can do about it now.

notes.title: Mirrors and their problems
notes.content:
Looks like we haven't posted any news during the last time. Let's fix it: we're trying to figure out possible ways of improving performance of mirrors on the stations. In Metro Simulator 2, we use HDRP renderer which provides better picture, but it also more resource-taxing.

Mirrors affect performance dramatically, and we are working on looking for ways to fix this problem. If we don't succeed, we'll go on one of two ways: either disable mirrors completely or make them optional so that you can enable them if you have a quite powerful PC.

notes.title: About Nomernoy's systems
notes.content:
We're hardly working on scripting the "Nomernoy" train, and today we'll tell you about the things we have already implemented and what we are working on now.

[h2]Driver's controller and acceleration system[/h2]

We have already spoke about the global re-work of train controls in Metro Simulator 2, which gave us a possibility to create individual control systems. Oka got an optimized system, Russia got a re-worked system of acceleration with a new mechanism of driver's controller. Now, Nomernoy has got an individual mechanism - rheostat controller.
To be short, rheostat controller is a mechanism which allows the train to accelerate and brake fluently. It has 36 position for acceleration and 18 for braking. The higher the position, the more intensive the train accelerates or slows down.
Positions for accelerations serve two purposes depending on from which positions we switched it - making the train accelerate faster (when moving it up) and making it accelerate slower (when moving it down).
Decelerating works in two options - Bypass, when you need to manually move the rheostat controller between T-1 and T-1a states, and automatic in T-2 state, when rheostat controller automatically decelerates.

[h2]Pneumatic system[/h2]

Pneumatics have an individual place in train's technical composition, but we haven't been able to implement them up to a recent time. But, when we decided to make Nomernoy, we decided to make it due to absolute necessity of this system in this train.
The main control of pneumatic train in Nomernoy train is the independent brakes 013 (КрМ) It has 7 positions to adjust braking force, with the last position being emergency brake. It's initialized by the uncoupling cap, and you won't be able to drive the train without it. Pneumatic system is connected to ARS (Automatic Speed Control System). If you drive past the red traffic light or start driving without allowing frequency without Vigilance pedal, brake system will be automatically set to Emergency position, and the train will stop.

We'll share more details about the development while we are working on the game. Don't forget to add the game to your wishlist in order not to skip other news about the game and its Early Access release in the first half of this year.

notes.title: About new train movement system in Metro Simulator 2
notes.content:
The most noticeable part when driving a train is movement physics. Our programmers re-worked this system for Metro Simulator 2.

Now, when movement physics system has several parts which execute after each other, we can see that the train moves correctly.

Imagine water which is travelling through a multi-layer filter. The same happens with acceleration and speed. We needed to pass them through different "filters" such as slope angle, engine power, manual controller state (for Oka train), applied traction force (for Russia train), state of rheostat controller (for older Soviet train) etc. As a result, we get a very realistic train behavior model.

We're almost done re-working this system's scripts for Oka train. Also, we tested it on the new line. We'd like to mention that besides graphical part we improved optimization and improved train imitation on far distances.
